metadata.title: Earnings live updates: Duolingo stock jumps on user growth, upbeat guidance

content.text:
Earnings live updates: Duolingo stock jumps on user growth, upbeat guidance
The third quarter earnings season is over halfway done, and the reports continue to pour in. This week brings another shot of major earnings courtesy of Apple (AAPL), Palantir (PLTR), and AMD (AMD).
Read more: Apple beats Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales but misses on China revenue
In addition to those tech heavyweights, investors will be watching for results out of Roku (ROKU), Arm Holdings (ARM), McDonald's (MCD), QUALCOMM (QCOM), Novo Nordisk (NVO), Uber Technologies (UBER), Toyota Motor Corporation (TM), ConocoPhillips (COP), and Moderna (MRNA).
S&P 500 corporations continue to demonstrate robust earnings growth. According to FactSet data, approximately 60% of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings, with an overall earnings growth rate of 30.2%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the index.
- Grace O'Donnell
AMD beats Q3 estimates as data center revenue climbs 97%
Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports:
AMD (AMD) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.
AMD stock climbed more than 4% following the news.
"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.
"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."
For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.
- Grace O'Donnell
Duolingo stock jumps as daily users surge, company raises guidance
Duolingo (DUOL) stock jumped 10% after the company reported that its daily active users (DAUs) rose 29% year over year to 64.9 million. Paid subscribers for the language learning platform grew 14% annually to 13.1 million.
165.80 +37.80 (+29.53%)As of 9:59:59 AM EST. Market Open.But the company is eyeing stronger user growth as it targets a goal of 1 billion users. Duolingo said its operating expenses increased 24% year over year. Those expenses included $11.4 million that the company set aside for a company-wide performance bonus for employees if it achieves DAU growth of 25% or greater in Q4.
Here's what Duolingo reported in Q3, versus estiamtes compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
-
Revenue: $309 million, up 12% year over year, versus estimates of $303 million
-
Earnings per share: $0.58, versus estimates of $0.56
-
Guidance: Raised across all key financial metrics. Revenue is expected at $1.22 billion, ahead of the Street's forecast of $1.20 billion
"We expect to finish 2026 at the high end of both the 10% to 12% bookings growth and 15% to 18% revenue growth targets we set at the start of the year. We expect full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $323 million, or a 26.5% margin, up $3 million from our previous guidance, and $21 million above the midpoint of our original 2026 guidance provided in February," the company stated.
-
- Grace O'Donnell
Super Micro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook
Yahoo Finance's Daniel Howley reports:
Data center infrastructure company Super Micro (SMCI) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.
The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.
Super Micro stock rose more than 5% immediately following the news.
"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.
"DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time and more cost-effective for our customer base."
- Grace O'Donnell
Pfizer focuses on GLP-1, oncology drug development as COVID product sales decline
Pfizer (PFE) stock fell slightly on Tuesday despite reporting an earnings beat and upbeat guidance. The pharmaceutical company said it saw operational revenue growth contributions from several treatments, including Eliquis, Paxlovid, the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec, and Lorbrena, during the quarter, though its COVID-19 products declined.
In the earnings call, Pfizer said it expects to spend $10.8 billion-$11.8 billion on research and development this year, particularly on developing its oncology and obesity pipeline. Pfizer is working on berobenatide, a GLP-1 injectable administered only once a month rather than weekly, as well as several cancer drugs.
"Pfizer had another strong quarter with commercial momentum and disciplined execution while advancing our strategy for creating long-term shareholder value," CEO Albert Bourla said in a release. "Our obesity program continued to advance and recent milestones in oncology, immunology and vaccines further demonstrate the potential of our pipeline."
In the third quarter, Pfizer reported revenue was little changed year over year at $16.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $15.9 billion, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Earnings per share came in at $0.56, beating Wall Street's estimates of $0.48 per share.
Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion, up from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. The company also raised and narrowed its 2026 earnings per share guidance to $2.95 to $3.05.
- Ines Ferré
Shopify stock tanks as Q3 revenue, total order value miss Wall Street estimates
Shopify (SHOP) stock plunged 7% on Tuesday after reporting third quarter results that missed the mark on several key metrics.
The cloud-based e-commerce platform's Q3 revenue of $3.74 billion came in just shy of consensus estimates of $3.75 billion for the first time since 2022, according to Bloomberg data. Subscription revenue for the quarter of $836 million also missed Wall Street expectations of $850.2 million, raising concerns about growth in its main recurring-revenue business.
Gross merchandise volume, or the total dollar value of orders sold through Shopify's platform, was $119.15 billion, also falling short of estimates of $120.08 billion.
Shopify's adjusted earnings per share of $0.49 topped estimates of $0.48.
- Grace O'Donnell
Apple tops Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales, but misses on China revenue
Apple (AAPL) stock is declining in extended trading after beating on earnings but missing on China revenue.
Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports on the quarter:
Apple reported its fourth quarter earnings after the bell on Monday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines on strong iPhone sales.
This is Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus, who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.
For the quarter, Apple reported earnings per share (EPS) of $2.10 on revenue of $114.48 billion. Wall Street was looking for EPS of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates.
The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.
Read live updates and analysis from the quarter and earnings call >
- Grace O'Donnell
Roku sales grow 24% year over year ahead of Fox acquisition
Roku (ROKU) reported a substantial earnings beat on Monday, driven by its ninth straight quarter of double-digit advertising growth.
Here's what Roku reported, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
-
Revenue: up 24% year over year to $1.5 billion, versus estimates of $1.41 billion.
-
Advertising revenue grew 23% YoY to $727 million.
-
Subscriptions revenue grew 23% YoY to $581 million.
-
-
Earnings per share: $1.20, versus estimates of $0.55.
-
Guidance: None given.
Roku stock was little changed following the report.
In June, Roku entered an agreement to be acquired by Fox (FOX). The company said that, in light of its pending takeover, it would not host an earnings call or provide a forecast.
"Our third quarter demonstrated that we succeed when our partners succeed, whether it is a streaming service gaining subscribers through Premium Subscriptions, a content company monetizing its library on The Roku Channel, an advertiser buying through a third-party DSP, or a TV brand choosing the Roku TV OS," CEO Anthony Wood wrote in a press release.
-
- Grace O'Donnell
Palantir raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales accelerate
Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reports:
Palantir (PLTR) beat Wall Street estimates on its third quarter revenue and profit on Monday and raised its full-year revenue outlook as the data software company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever.
Palantir reported Q3 revenue of $2.313 billion, a 96% increase from the previous year. Wall Street had expected revenue of $2.17 billion, according to Bloomberg data.
Palantir now sees full-year revenue between $8.530 billion and $8.534 billion, topping analyst estimates of $8.2 billion. The company also raised its US commercial sales target to more than $3.559 billion. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 also beat consensus estimates of $0.40.
